messages.author: Zornik
messages.content_text:
Date: 1/05/2026

Session: New york am

HT Bias: We rallied 240 ish point of new york open, taking out ATH, making me a little sceptical whether 10am would continue ripping up. What I wanted to see was an smt at the highs, followed by some sort of rb, holding the smt.

LT Bias: We intially formed the smtn but es formed 3 equal highs so that first smt was not valid. After es took those out we formed a new one wich I liked better. We know also formed a 5m rb.

Entry Confluences (minimum 3): We had an smt at the highs, formed a 5m rb of the smt, we tapped the ce of that 5rb, I entered on the 1m rb tapping the ce. My target was the start of the 5m imbalance. I was hesitant to be more greedy but decided that at ath's, this was a point price could retrace back to my entry.

Entry Time: 10:24

SL: 9.50 point stop

RR: 4.87 (I meant to do 5 but kinda messed up here.)

Confidence: Pretty confident I'd give it a 6.5

Mental State during trade: Pretty good, went BE after hitting 3 RR. After that I putted 2 alerts, one at the BE and one at the TP. We also delivered it in 8 minutes so that kept me low stress.

Mental state after trade/session: After seeing it dump that hard, and realising I could have passed my eval halfway in this trade, I felt kinda left out, felt like I needed to work on placing my tp's. However I did not trade anymore, closed my laptop and just reflected on my win.

Result: Win

Lesson: It was a 5 RR trade with not a real clear draw. Taking tp at the start of the imbalance was not a bad idea. One win, done for the day. Nice bounce back from a very weird psychology week with bad thoughts, lets make this the new normal.

Did I follow my rules: Yes (ofc its easy when you win...) Day 1 complete  (edited)
